headline: Morning fog and a few storms precede a sharp Kentucky cool-down; the Upstate stays hot through Friday before a dry, gusty front
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Dense fog is the immediate concern around Danville and Lexington this morning. After fog lifts, Central Kentucky enters the warm sector with a few showers or thunderstorms possible this afternoon; any storm could produce a locally strong gust, but coverage should remain scattered. A strong cold front crosses Friday, bringing gusty west-to-northwest winds, a few showers and falling temperatures. Saturday is much cooler, with clearing followed by a growing frost and localized freeze risk Saturday night.

currentConditions.note: The observation contained valid fog and visibility fields but no valid temperature or dewpoint; missing values were excluded from temperature adjustment.

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: OFFICIAL: NWS Louisville Special Weather Statement for Boyle County through 8 AM EDT for patchy dense fog and visibility as low as one-quarter mile. INDEPENDENT: a few afternoon storms may produce lightning, brief heavy rain and an isolated strong wind gust.
days.forecast: Fog and low clouds dominate the morning, locally dense near Lexington and in sheltered valleys. Conditions improve late morning, then partial heating supports scattered showers and thunderstorms from early afternoon into early evening. Many locations receive little or no rain, but a storm that does form may briefly produce heavy rain and a strong gust. South to southwest flow increases tonight ahead of the front.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: The Thursday-morning Special Weather Statement was active at issuance but expires before this period. Independent forecast concern shifts to west-to-northwest gusts around 22–32 mph and rapidly falling afternoon temperatures.
days.forecast: The day's highest readings may occur near or before daybreak, around the upper 60s to lower 70s, as the cold front crosses. Temperatures then fall through the afternoon. A band of scattered showers is most likely from late morning through late afternoon, but rainfall should remain light. West winds turn northwest and become gusty, and readings fall into the 40s Friday night.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: The Thursday-morning Special Weather Statement was active at issuance but expires before this period. Independent concern is widespread frost Saturday night, with a localized freeze possible in colder rural locations.
days.forecast: A stray early shower cannot be ruled out, then clouds decrease as much colder and drier air settles in. North winds remain brisk during the day. Mostly clear conditions and easing wind Saturday night support widespread frost; the coldest rural and sheltered locations may reach freezing.

kentucky.bottomLine: Dense fog is the immediate Kentucky hazard. A few afternoon storms are possible, but coverage should be scattered. Friday brings the decisive change—gusty winds, a few showers and falling temperatures—followed by a chilly Saturday and frost or a localized freeze Saturday night.
kentucky.confidence: High on morning fog and the Friday–Saturday cool-down; moderate on today's exact storm coverage and Friday shower timing; moderate-high on Saturday-night frost

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: The Clemson–Central area remains dry and unusually warm through Friday. Patchy lake or river fog may occur briefly this morning, but sunshine should dominate afterward. A strong cold front crosses Friday night into early Saturday with little moisture. Its main effects are a gusty wind shift and a 20–25 degree temperature drop for Saturday, followed by a chilly Saturday night.

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert at issuance. Independent concern is limited to brief patchy lake or river fog through about 10 AM and near-record afternoon warmth.
days.forecast: Patchy shallow fog near lakes and rivers dissipates by midmorning. Otherwise, expect sunshine, light south-southwest wind and very warm afternoon temperatures. The air mass remains too dry for showers. Mostly clear and mild conditions continue tonight.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert at issuance. Independent concern is west-to-northwest gusts around 20–30 mph with the dry frontal passage late Friday and Friday night.
days.forecast: Sunny and very warm ahead of the front. Southwest winds strengthen during the afternoon, then turn west to northwest during the evening and night. Moisture is limited, so most of the area should remain dry. Temperatures fall sharply behind the front overnight.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert at issuance. Independent concern is a gusty north wind early and a chilly Saturday night; frost risk is mainly north and west of Clemson but cannot be ruled out in colder sheltered spots.
days.forecast: A brief early shower is possible near the front, but most locations remain dry. Skies become mostly sunny while north winds usher in much cooler air. Saturday night is mostly clear and chilly, with the coldest sheltered locations dipping into the upper 30s.

upstate.bottomLine: Dry, sunny and very warm weather continues through Friday. The front should pass with little rain, but gusty winds and a sharp temperature drop follow Friday night. Saturday is sunny, breezy and much cooler, with a chilly night to follow.
upstate.confidence: High on dry weather and the temperature reversal; moderate-high on Friday-night frontal timing and gust strength; moderate on isolated Saturday-morning shower and frost potential

sourceNotes: OFFICIAL ALERT: NWS Louisville Special Weather Statement was active for Boyle County at 7:15 AM EDT and expires at 8:00 AM EDT, warning of patchy dense fog and visibility as low as one-quarter mile. No official NWS alert was active at the Upstate point.
The KDVK observation reported fog/mist and 3-mile visibility but supplied no valid temperature or dewpoint. Those missing values were excluded; the forecast did not convert them to 32°F.

College of DuPage radar at 7:10 AM EDT showed no meaningful precipitation over the Upstate and mainly weak/scattered returns around the forecast corridor, with the more organized precipitation displaced west/northwest. True-color satellite at 7:11 AM showed a broader cloud/fog field over the Ohio Valley and clearer conditions farther southeast.

ECMWF point guidance is materially wetter than GFS/HRRR for Kentucky today. The NWS point forecast and Louisville discussion support scattered rather than widespread coverage, so the candidate uses a 20–40% range and moderate confidence while retaining the ECMWF solution as the wet upper bound.

SPC's 12Z Day 1 outlook places a broad Marginal Risk from the mid-Mississippi into the Ohio Valley. NWS Louisville's local analysis identifies isolated strong/severe wind gusts as the primary Central Kentucky concern and says the more favorable tornado threat should miss the forecast area.
HRRR, RAP, NAM, NAM 3-km Nest, GFS, GEFS and ECMWF run availability was verified from official directories; College of DuPage panels supplied a common visual analysis source.
Tempest data was not used for Upstate observations, verification, calibration or adjustment.
Official NWS alerts are separate from this independent analysis. Independent hazard probabilities do not constitute watches or warnings.
